{{Short description|Adjunction between a category of co/presheaf under the co/Yoneda embedding}}
{{CS1 config|mode=cs2}}

In mathematics, '''Isbell conjugacy''' (a.k.a. '''Isbell duality''' or '''Isbell adjunction''') (named after [[John R. Isbell]]{{R|Baez2022}}<ref>{{harv|Di Liberti
|2020|loc=2. Isbell duality}}</ref>) is a fundamental construction of [[enriched category theory]] formally introduced by [[William Lawvere]] in 1986.<ref name =Lawvere1986>{{harv|Lawvere|1986|page=169}}</ref><ref>{{harv|Rutten|1998}}</ref> That is a duality between covariant and contravariant representable [[Presheaf (category theory)|presheave]]s associated with an objects of categories under the Yoneda embedding.<ref>{{harv|Melliès|Zeilberger|2018}}</ref><ref>{{harv|Willerton|2013}}</ref> In addition, Lawvere<ref>{{harv|Lawvere|1986|page=169}}</ref> says; "Then the conjugacies are the first step toward expressing the duality between space and quantity fundamental to mathematics".<ref>{{harv|Space and quantity in nlab}}</ref>

== Definition ==
=== Yoneda embedding ===
The (covariant) [[Yoneda embedding]] is a [[covariant functor]] from a small category <math>\mathcal{A}</math> into the [[category of presheaves]] <math>\left[\mathcal{A}^{op}, \mathcal{V} \right]</math> on <math>\mathcal{A}</math>, taking <math>X \in \mathcal{A}</math> to the contravariant [[representable functor]]: {{R|Baez2022}}<ref name=nlab2>{{harv|Yoneda embedding in nlab}}
</ref><ref>{{harv|Awodey|2006|loc= Definition 8.1.}}</ref>

<math>y  \; (h^{\bullet}) :\mathcal{A} \rightarrow  \left[\mathcal{A}^{op}, \mathcal{V} \right]</math> 

<math>X \mapsto \mathrm{hom} (-,X).</math>

and the co-Yoneda  embedding{{R|Baez2022}}{{R|nlab1}} (a.k.a. dual Yoneda embedding<ref>{{harv|Day|Lack|2007|loc=§9. Isbell conjugacy}}</ref>)  is a [[contravariant functor]] from a small category <math>\mathcal{A}</math> into the [[Opposite category#Properties|opposite]] of the [[category of co-presheaves]] <math>\left[\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{V} \right]^{op}</math> on <math>\mathcal{A}</math>, taking <math>X \in \mathcal{A}</math> to the covariant representable functor: 

<math>z \; ({h_{\bullet}}^{op}): \mathcal{A} \rightarrow \left[\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{V} \right]^{op}</math>

<math>X \mapsto \mathrm{hom} (X,-).</math>

=== Isbell duality ===
[[File:Isbell duality.svg|thumb|Origin of symbols <math>\mathcal{O}</math> (“[[ring of functions]]”) and <math>\mathrm{Spec}</math> (“spectrum”): {{harvtxt|Lawvere|1986|page=169}}{{Failed verification|date=May 2025}} says that; "<math>\mathcal{O}</math>" assigns to each general space the algebra of functions on it, whereas "<math>\mathrm{Spec}</math>" assigns to each algebra its “spectrum” which is a general space. ]]
[[File:Nerve and realization (ver. left kan extension).svg|thumb|note:In order for this commutative diagram to hold, it is required that <math>\mathcal{A}</math> is small and E is co-complete.<ref>{{harv|Di Liberti
|2020|loc=Remark 2.3 (The (co)nerve construction).}}</ref><ref>{{harv|Kelly|1982|loc=Proposition 4.33 }}</ref><ref>{{harv|Riehl|2016|loc=Remark 6.5.9.}}</ref><ref>{{harv|Imamura|2022|loc=Theorem 2.4 }}</ref>]]
Every functor <math>F \colon \mathcal{A}^\mathrm{op}\to \mathcal{V}</math> has an Isbell conjugate of a functor{{R|Baez2022}} <math>F^{\ast} \colon \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{V}</math>, given by

<math>F^{\ast} (X) = \mathrm{hom} (F , y(X)).</math> 

In contrast, every functor <math>G \colon \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{V}</math> has an Isbell conjugate of a functor{{R|Baez2022}} <math>G^{\ast} \colon \mathcal{A}^\mathrm{op} \to \mathcal{V}</math> given by

<math>G^{\ast} (X) = \mathrm{hom} (z(X) , G).</math>

These two functors are not typically inverses, or even [[natural isomorphism]]s. Isbell duality asserts that the relationship between these two functors is an adjunction.{{R|Baez2022}}

'''Isbell duality''' is the relationship between Yoneda embedding and co-Yoneda embedding；

Let <math>\mathcal{V}</math> be a [[closed monoidal category|symmetric monoidal closed category]], and let <math>\mathcal{A}</math> be a small category enriched in <math>\mathcal{V}</math>.

The '''Isbell duality''' is an [[Adjunction (category theory)|adjunction]] between the functor categories; <math>\left(\mathcal{O} \dashv \mathrm{Spec} \right) \colon \left[\mathcal{A}^{op}, \mathcal{V} \right] {\underset{\mathrm{Spec}}{\overset{\mathcal{O}}{\rightleftarrows}}} 
  \left[\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{V} \right]^{op}</math>.<ref name=Baez2022>{{harv|Baez
|2022}}</ref>{{R|Lawvere1986}}<ref name=nlab1>{{harv|Isbell duality in nlab}}</ref><ref name=DiLiberti2020>{{harv|Di Liberti
|2020|loc=Remark 2.4}}</ref><ref>{{harv|Fosco
|2021}}</ref>

Applying the nerve construction, the functors <math>\mathcal{O} \dashv \mathrm{Spec}</math> of Isbell duality are such that <math>\mathcal{O}  \cong \mathrm{Lan_{y}z}</math> and <math>\mathrm{Spec} \cong \mathrm{Lan_{z}y}</math>.{{R|DiLiberti2020}}<ref>{{harv|Di Liberti |Loregian|2019|loc=Lemma 5.13.}}</ref><ref group=note>For the symbol '''Lan''', see left [[Kan extension]].</ref>
